finish.summary:
I built a small shelf unit with two drawers, but I can't give it a 50 kg rating. The configurator only checks that parts fit and don't collide. It can't tell how much weight printed plastic will hold.

The bottom row has a full base with a half base on each side, and each half base holds a drawer. Two more full bases are stacked on the centre base, and a cover on top makes a shelf. I put a stack of books on that top shelf to show what it's for.

The open faces got solid end caps, except four I left open toward the front of the two upper bases so books can go in. All the joints are bolted. The checks pass and no parts collide. It comes to 41 parts and an estimated 2.3 kg of filament.

One limit: the configurator wouldn't place bases beside the stack above the bottom row, so storage space is small. Only the top shelf took a book prop. A book laid on a drawer was refused because it overlapped the wall of the base above.

M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
